skills.name: Credit creation: the loan and deposit entry

note.text: When a bank grants a loan by crediting an account, it records a loan asset and matching deposit liability. The borrower has a new deposit asset and loan debt. This creates deposit money, not equal net wealth or new physical resources. Spending can move the deposit to another person or bank; settlement then matters. Repayment of principal from a deposit reduces both the loan and deposit in the simplified entry. Interest and fees are separate events. Real lending remains constrained by risk, capital, liquidity, demand and monetary conditions.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to trace a new bank loan and matching deposit without confusing money creation with wealth creation. Builds on: bank assets, liabilities and equity. Leads to: the assumptions of the simplified deposit-expansion model.

sections.heading: Follow the local case
sections.text: Original new loan: {4000} CFA francs credited to a borrower. Bank loan assets rise by {4000}; deposit liabilities rise by {4000}; equity is unchanged by this principal-only entry. The borrower’s deposit and debt rise together. Subsequent transfer, interest and repayment need separate entries rather than being silently combined.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Write the bank’s asset and liability changes, then the borrower’s asset and debt changes. Track the event and perspective before calculating. Do not say banks merely move a particular saver’s labelled notes or that recording a loan removes all lending limits.

the obligation matching the borrower’s new loan funds

cards.idea: Use the stated case evidence to identify the economic feature.
example: Granting and crediting the loan expands both sides.
The borrower’s deposit rises alongside a repayment obligation.
Principal paid from a deposit extinguishes that part of the loan and deposit.
A matching deposit and debt do not create equal net wealth.

cards.idea: Explain a consequence instead of assuming every option has the same effect.
example: paired creation: It also owes the new deposit.
borrower debt: The loan remains repayable under its terms.
principal repayment: The stated entry reduces, rather than originates, the claim.
money versus wealth: A financial entry is not physical production.

questions.prompt: A fictional bank’s loan assets are {l} CFA francs before it grants and credits a new loan of {x}. No repayments, write-downs or other changes occur. What are its loan assets afterwards?

misconceptions.explain: The granted loan adds to the lender’s loan claim in this case.
That omits the stated existing loan assets.

solution: The new loan increases the bank’s claim on borrowers by {x}.
Loan assets become {l} + {x} = {answer} CFA francs; a matching deposit liability is created at origination.
